newsitem.title: UK: Vernons Pools axes further 90 UK jobs.
newsitem.headline: Vernons Pools axes further 90 UK jobs.

text.p: Vernons Pools said on Wednesday that it intended to cut 70 people from the workforce at its Merseyside headquarters and was reducing its national sales force by 20.
The plans mean that Vernons Merseyside workforce will have been cut from 1045 people to 410 since the launch of the National Lottery in 1994.
Vernons, owned by betting and hotels group Ladbroke Group Plc, said that the soccer pools market has halved in size since the lottery was launched.

"I am bitterly disappointed by the need for these new job losses. We have had to take these steps to ensure the long-term viability of the business," said Vernons Pools managing director Phil Jarrold.
"We hope the next Parliament will agree changes to the law so that long-odds gaming is taxed on the same basis as other consumer products," he added.
Pools betting duty is 26.5 percent, compared with a standard VAT rate of 17.5 percent.

The pools companies are also lobbying for the right to run midweek games and to extend pools competitions to other sport such as rugby union and cricket. They would also like to be able to pay out small winnings over the counter in shops.
